title: RFID Silicone Keyfob — Medical & Food-Contact IP68
summary: RFID silicone keyfobs encapsulate an HF or LF inlay in platinum-cured PDMS, sealed to IP68 per IEC 60529 for continuous immersion. The compound is ISO 10993-1 / -5 / -10 biocompatible, USP Class VI cleared, and FDA 21 CFR 177.2600 + LFGB § 31 food-contact compliant with EN 1186 migration testing. Shore A 40-70 hand-feel and a -40 °C to +230 °C operating range target aquatic centres, gyms, food plants and paediatric / healthcare facilities.

sections.title: Where a silicone keyfob is the only credential that survives the duty cycle
bullets: Aquatic centres, water parks and spas — 1-10 ppm free chlorine, 1-5 ppm bromine, continuous wet-handling. Silicone's Si-O backbone is chemically inert where PVC plasticises and ABS mould-lines admit water within 3-12 months.

24-hour gyms and wellness studios — sweat pH 4.5-7.0, sauna cycling 80-95 °C, drops onto rubber gym flooring. Silicone's -40 °C to +230 °C range and Shore A 60 flex absorb the envelope without cracking.

Food processing and commercial kitchens — IP69K daily wash-down with hot-caustic (1-2 % NaOH, 60-80 °C), peracetic acid (80-150 ppm), chlorinated-alkaline cleaners. Silicone with moulded-in stainless ring (no glued seam) is the only credential with no water-ingress path.

Paediatric, daycare and healthcare facilities — skin-contact programmes where the credential is mouthed, chewed, or worn on a wrist for an 8-12 h shift. USP Class VI + ISO 10993 biocompatibility plus LFGB / 21 CFR 177.2600 food-contact chemistry clears the hygienic envelope.

Outdoor residential / campus / ski-resort access — UV exposure, thermal cycling (-30 °C winter to +60 °C black-asphalt summer), ice contact. Silicone's UV resistance (no yellowing, no chalking) and thermal tolerance outlast commodity ABS by 3-5× in the same duty.

sections.intro: Shore A 40-70 tunable; default Shore A 60 ± 5 matches silicone-wristband feel for mixed-credential programmes. Below 40: deforms around the split ring; above 70: loses shock-absorption advantage over rigid ABS.
bullets: Single-colour or dual-colour two-shot moulding in any PMS; pad-print / silkscreen / laser marking with silicone-compatible ink. Debossed / embossed 3D logo moulded into the cavity; embedded dome-label covered by clear silicone overcap for full-colour branding.

Stainless steel split ring (304 / 316) moulded in; lobster clasp optional; plated-steel rings banned in the spec sheet — they rust in pool / marine within 6-12 months. Snag-free single-moulded profile — no crimped lanyards, no adhesive-bonded strap ends that can delaminate.

sections.title: Platinum-cured vs peroxide-cured — why the spec line matters
bullets: Platinum-cured PDMS (our default) uses a platinum catalyst addition cure: no peroxide byproducts, no residual siloxanes to leach, clears USP Class VI + ISO 10993 + EN 1186 food-contact migration with margin.

Peroxide-cured silicone uses dicumyl-peroxide cure: 0.5-1.5 % residual decomposition products remain in the matrix and can migrate; disqualified for paediatric, medical, food-contact and pharma-ancillary programmes.

Cost delta platinum vs peroxide is ≈ 15-25 % of compound cost (≈ $0.08-0.15 per keyfob) — negligible next to the labour of re-qualifying a programme that failed migration testing at LFGB retail audit.

Low-grade industrial-silicone compound (non-food-grade, peroxide-cure, unknown pigment chemistry) is cheaper still — but cannot legally enter EU / US food-contact or medical channels, and is explicitly flagged on the DoC we ship.

The spec line "platinum-cured medical-grade silicone, ISO 10993-5 / -10 pass, USP Class VI, 21 CFR 177.2600 + LFGB § 31, EN 1186 ≤ 10 mg/dm²" is the shortest copy-paste that closes the chemistry audit for any serious programme.

before: Plasticiser migration (phthalates), UV chalking, mould-line water ingress; 1-3 year field life in wet / outdoor duty.
Not cleared for USP Class VI; fails ISO 10993-10 sensitisation on some pigment lots; disqualified for paediatric + healthcare + food-contact.
EN 1186 overall-migration often > 10 mg/dm² on olive-oil simulant; LFGB § 31 decorated-side migration fails on pigment bleed.
Welded / adhesive-bonded seam creates an ingress path — failure mode is chip-pad corrosion at 6-18 months in IP69K wash-down.
after: Platinum-cured PDMS — Si-O inert backbone, no plasticiser / peroxide byproducts, 5-10 year field life with no chalking.
USP Class VI cleared + ISO 10993-1 / -5 / -10 pass + LFGB § 31 + FDA 21 CFR 177.2600; fit for paediatric, healthcare, pharma-ancillary, food-plant.
EN 1186 overall-migration ≤ 10 mg/dm² on all three simulants (olive oil, 50 % ethanol, 3 % acetic acid) — cleared with margin.
Single-moulded body with stainless ring moulded in — no seam, no glue, no ingress path; IP68 continuous + IP69K wash-down for life.

sections.title: Field-duty record — what 5-year aquatic and food-plant programmes actually see
bullets: 14,000-member aquatic-centre chain (5-year field data): silicone + DESFire EV2 keyfob failure rate 0.3 %/year. ABS + MIFARE Classic predecessor was 9-12 %/year failure rate, driven by water ingress at the mould line.

Commercial-kitchen programme at a regional QSR operator (3-year field data): moulded-in stainless-ring silicone fob survived daily hot-caustic + peracetic wash-down indefinitely. ABS predecessor had a 22 % 18-month failure rate at the welded seam.

Paediatric-hospital visitor-credential programme (2-year field data): ISO 10993-cleared silicone fob passed infection-control audit and autoclave cycling (134 °C / 18 min) for reissue. PVC predecessor had been retired after LFGB audit flagged phthalate migration.

European retail-gym chain (4-year field data): silicone fob with pad-printed logo survived 4-5 sauna cycles / day + sweat + outdoor UV with no silkscreen fade or chalking. ABS predecessor had UV-yellowed within 18 months and lost 15-20 % of units to cracking at the ring-hole.

Ski-resort lift-access programme: silicone fob with Shore A 60 body + stainless split ring survived -30 °C to +60 °C daily cycling + glove-handling for 6+ seasons. Moulded-in ring eliminated the 12-18 % annual loss-rate the prior ABS fob incurred at the welded lanyard crimp.

sections.title: How to roll out a silicone keyfob programme without failing a chemistry or PACS audit
bullets: Specify platinum-cured medical-grade silicone explicitly — do not accept "food-grade silicone" without a supplier declaration naming the cure chemistry; peroxide-cured compound disqualifies paediatric / medical / pharma-ancillary programmes.

Close the chemistry audit: ISO 10993-1 / -5 / -10 biocompatibility, USP Class VI where pharma-ancillary, FDA 21 CFR 177.2600 + LFGB § 31 food-contact, EN 1186 overall-migration ≤ 10 mg/dm², RoHS 3 DoC, REACH SVHC screen, California Prop 65 disclosure. All are declared on every ≥ MOQ 500 shipment.
Spec 304 or 316 stainless split ring moulded into the silicone body — plated-steel rings rust in pool and marine within 6-12 months and stain the body; cost differential is < $0.05 per unit.

Don't use CRYPTO-1 MIFARE Classic in a new silicone rollout — the IP68 housing is engineered for a decade in the field. Pair it with MIFARE Plus SE SL1 migration mode or DESFire EV2 / EV3 AES-128 from day one, or NTAG 424 DNA SUN if you want tap-to-reveal or anti-cloning.

Stock moulds (round Ø 35 mm, oval 45 × 30 mm, rectangle 40 × 25 mm) and differentiate via PMS colour + silkscreen / pad-print. Custom tooling (~$1,500-3,500) only makes sense above 1,000 units; below that, per-fob amortised cost exceeds stock mould by 3-5×.

Commission PACS integration and IP68 soak-test in the pilot: a 72-h continuous-immersion test at 1.0 m in chlorinated water mirrors the duty cycle. Expect zero read failures on a correctly moulded programme.

faq.question: Can a silicone keyfob survive long-term chlorinated pool water?
faq.answer: Yes — platinum-cured polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) silicone is chemically inert against 1-10 ppm free chlorine, 1-5 ppm bromine, hydrogen peroxide, isopropanol and quaternary-ammonium disinfectants. The moulded-in stainless split ring and seamless single-mould body eliminate the ingress path that fails ABS and PVC keyfobs at the welded seam. Five-year field data on a 14,000-member aquatic-centre programme shows 0.3 %/year failure rate versus 9-12 %/year on the ABS predecessor.

faq.question: Is the silicone safe for paediatric, healthcare and food-contact environments?
faq.answer: Yes — the default compound is platinum-cured medical-grade silicone cleared for skin, food and pharma-ancillary contact. It passes ISO 10993-1 biological evaluation, ISO 10993-5 cytotoxicity, ISO 10993-10 irritation and sensitisation, USP Class VI pharma-contact (acute systemic / intracutaneous / implantation), FDA 21 CFR 177.2600 rubber-articles-for-repeated-use food-contact, LFGB § 31 (Germany) food-contact and EN 1186 overall-migration ≤ 10 mg/dm². It is RoHS 3 and REACH compliant, latex-free, BPA-free, PVC-free, and California Prop 65 declared. For paediatric, daycare and pharmacy programmes specify the full biocompatibility + migration evidence pack as a line item on the PO.

faq.question: Does silicone attenuate the read range compared to plastic?
faq.answer: No — silicone is RF-transparent at both 13.56 MHz HF and 125 kHz LF, so read range matches an ABS or epoxy body of the same inlay: 3-5 cm tap at HF, 5-8 cm tap at LF for the standard inlay sizes. The antenna design and chip determine range, not the housing material. PACS integration, Wiegand / OSDP behaviour and access-control logic are identical to non-silicone form factors.

faq.question: Should I specify platinum-cured or peroxide-cured silicone?
faq.answer: Platinum-cured for any programme that touches skin, food, or pharma-ancillary duty. Platinum-cured PDMS has no residual peroxide decomposition products and clears USP Class VI + ISO 10993 + EN 1186 + LFGB with margin. Peroxide-cured compound retains 0.5-1.5 % residual byproducts that can migrate and disqualify the programme at migration audit. The cost delta is ≈ $0.08-0.15 per keyfob — far less than re-qualification cost on a failed retail / hospital audit. We ship the cure chemistry on the DoC so procurement can verify.

faq.question: Should I specify MIFARE Classic or upgrade to DESFire / NTAG 424 DNA in a silicone keyfob?
faq.answer: Upgrade. The IP68 silicone housing is engineered for 5-10 years in the field; the CRYPTO-1 cipher used in MIFARE Classic has been publicly broken since 2008 and cannot be patched. For new rollouts specify MIFARE Plus SE in SL1 / SL3 migration mode (same 4-byte UID so no reader change), DESFire EV2 / EV3 with AES-128 for authenticated access, or NTAG 424 DNA with SUN tap-to-reveal for anti-cloning and mobile-wallet integration — these chip families match the 5-10 year housing life and stay secure through 2035+.
